topic: Smart Pointers and Automatic Resource Management
explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr are used to manage dynamic resources automatically, ensuring proper cleanup and preventing memory leaks. They follow the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom, which ties resource lifetime to object lifetime. This approach simplifies resource management, especially in the presence of exceptions, by automatically releasing resources when the smart pointer goes out of scope, eliminating the need for manual delete calls.
syntax:
std::unique_ptr<T> ptr = std::make_unique<T>(constructor_args); // for exclusive ownership
std::shared_ptr<T> ptr = std::make_shared<T>(constructor_args); // for shared ownership
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage a dynamically allocated Widget object. The make_unique function creates a unique_ptr that owns the Widget instance. When the process() function ends, the unique_ptr goes out of scope, automatically destroying the Widget object without explicit delete calls. This exemplifies modern C++ resource management idioms, ensuring exception safety and preventing memory leaks.
